name: The Church, Templars and Inquisition (Dark Ages)

pages.name: The Church, Templars and Inquisition (Dark Ages)

text.content:
Reference notes on the mortal institutions most likely to threaten or entangle a Dark Ages chronicle's Cainites, for Storyteller use in building antagonists and plot hooks circa AD 1230.

Mother Church

The Church is the dominant spiritual and temporal power in Dark Medieval Europe, framing mortal life from baptism to last rites and wielding excommunication as a political weapon even against kings. Latin is its official language; the pope in Rome sits atop cardinals, bishops, monastic orders, and priests. No Cainite fully escapes its influence — even those who disliked it in mortal life may feel a twinge at the threat of losing the sacraments. Vampires interact with the Church in every way from ruling through bishops to using it as a hunting ground, and vampire arrogance has more than once roused the suspicion of astute clergy.

The Templars

Properly the Poor Knights of Christ and the Holy Temple of Solomon, founded 1114 and recognized by the Church in 1128, answering only to the pope. Recognizable by white surcoats bearing the red crusader's cross. Rumor holds that their upper ranks include wizards who studied in the Holy Land, seeking King Solomon's reputed command over spirits and beasts, and that their chapter houses hoard occult lore, relics, and treasure. Their focus on reclaiming the Holy Land keeps them from becoming a direct, systemic threat to Cainites, though their wealth and knowledge would make them formidable if turned that way; some vampires even ride alongside them when it serves mutual purposes.

The Inquisition

By AD 1230 the Church is deeply unsettled by spreading heresy — the Cathars, the Bogomils, and others — and for the first time is organizing a proactive response rather than letting individual bishops handle accusations as they arise. This new Holy Office of the Inquisition is not yet fully formed; Dominican leaders are currently field-testing the concept against Cathar heresy in the Languedoc region of France. While heresy is its founding purpose, a faction within the Inquisition believes monsters and fiends stalking the night are a symptom of the same corruption, and a secret hunt for such creatures has quietly continued for decades under priests and holy warriors claiming papal authority — educated, faithful, and burning with righteous fury.

Other Faiths

  • Jews live in scattered, often walled and curfewed communities across Europe and Outremer, subject to forced conversion during the Reconquista, blamed as scapegoats for misfortune, and largely limited by Christian authorities to trades like money-lending (forbidden to Christians as usury). Only in Outremer do they find some relative peace, crusades permitting.
  • Pagan traditions persist alongside Christian practice in the countryside, and the Church often absorbs pagan festivals wholesale to ease conversion; Lithuania remains an openly pagan kingdom, and parts of the British Isles keep old rites alive. Practitioners of the old ways are the most common target of witchcraft accusations.
  • Islam dominates the Holy Land and, until the Reconquista, controlled large parts of Iberia; Muslim, Jewish, and Christian communities there once lived side by side. Templar occult knowledge is rumored to derive partly from Muslim libraries in the Holy Land, repositories of ancient wisdom.
  • Divergent Christian sects ("heresies" to Rome) hold significant ground: the Cathars in Languedoc, the Orthodox Church in Eastern Europe and the Byzantine ruins, and Armenian, Antiochan, and Coptic churches around the Fertile Crescent.

vtmlarp.source: Faith and Fire (Dark Ages Vampire), Chapter Seven: Allies and Antagonists
